name: Question 7
problem:
$$
U=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} & -\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}],\,Σ=[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,V=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} & -\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices shown above. Given that $A=UΣ{V}^{T}$ is a singular value decomposition of $A,$ find the pseudoinverse ${A}^{+}.$
worked_solution:
If $A=UΣ{V}^{T}$ is a singular value decomposition of $A,$ then the pseudoinverse of $A$ is given by

$$
V\,{Σ}^{+}\,{U}^{T},
$$

where ${Σ}^{+}$ is the pseudoinverse of $Σ.$

First, notice that

$$
V=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}],\,{Σ}^{+}=\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,{U}^{T}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{+} & =V\,{Σ}^{+}\,{U}^{T} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{25}[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{25}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{25}[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

If A=UΣVT is a singular value decomposition of A, then the pseudoinverse of A is given by

VΣ+UT,

where Σ+ is the pseudoinverse of Σ.

First, notice that

V=15[1−221],Σ+=15[1000],UT=15[12−21].

Therefore, we have

A+=VΣ+UT=15[1−221]⋅15[1000]⋅15[12−21]=125[1−221]⋅[1000]⋅[12−21]=125[1020]⋅[12−21]=125[1224].
